scope: Theorem 2.4 (Exact pure energy charge) of the manuscript “Quenched SLE₃ Universality for the Weak Random-Bond Ising Model” (preprints/Quenched-SLE3-Universality-for-the-Weak-Random-Bond-Ising-Model-October-5-2026/quenched-sle3-weak-random-bond-ising.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 dbf1578546653fc5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every bounded even local observable f, the limit Q(f) = κ−1 lim |x|→∞ |x|2 E0[fBx] (2.9) exists. It defines a linear functional that kills constants, is invariant under lattice translations and square symmetries, and satisfies Q(be) = 1. Pure transfer preserves Q exactly. If f is supported in Bs(x), then |Q(f)| ≤ Cs∥f∥∞. (2.10) For centered f and R ≥ 4s, ∥PR,xf∥∞ ≤ C(s/R)∥f∥∞. (2.11) If Q(f) = 0, the factor s/R improves to (s/R)u; it improves to (s/R)w if, after auxiliary integration, f is also invariant under quarter turns about x. More generally, with v = u or v = w according to these two symmetry classes, ∥PR,xf − Q(f)PR,xBx∥∞ ≤ C(s/R)v ∥f∥∞. (2.12) All constants are independent of s, R, and f.
